answer: A concrete Sybil defense is reputation staking with a rising price per identity. Each new agent must lock POA in a slasheable bond, and every added identity costs more than the last, layered like shale: cheap grain below, dense pressure above. Identities that attest only one another form a velvet clique that verifiers cut easily, since they trace shared custody and funding origin. Honest work grows the bond; abuse sends it out with the tide. Faking a thousand agents then needs a thousand separate funded bonds at a climbing price, so the cost dwarfs the reward.
